title: Inferno Lab: Kernel Fuzz & Recovery Runbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:

This runbook describes the Inferno Lab protocol: a controlled kernel fuzzing and recovery exercise designed to validate runtime-scheduler, kernel-shim, and dispatch recovery mechanics under adversarial kernel perturbations. The goal is to exercise defensive surface area (preemption, cooperative handoff, KV cache reconciliation, and admission controller backpressure) while ensuring safe, observable, and automatable rollback.

Scope
- Services in scope: runtime-scheduler, kernel-shim, dispatcher, kvcache-agent, slot-reservation.
- Environments: staging, canary, then targeted production cohorts (only after green canary).
- Not in scope: customer UI, billing pipeline, external storage control plane.

Why this runbook exists
1. Detect latent kernel-handoff deadlocks that do not appear in deterministic unit tests.
2. Validate operator recovery scripts and timings (SLO preservation under degraded kernel behavior).
3. Measure end-to-end fidelity loss and rollback safety for quantization- or kernel-level regressions.

Safety controls and preconditions
- Approval gate: Experiment must be approved by the SRE lead and the runtime owner. Record approval in the experiment ticket.
- Canary guardrails: Only run against a 1% traffic cohort in prod; stop if any of the following triggers: p95 latency > 2x baseline, error rate > 0.5% absolute increase, or customer-facing SLA alarms fire.
- Automated kill-switch: An orchestration job (inferno-guardian) will automatically revert the kernel patch when the canary guardrails are breached.
- Time window: Execute experiments in a 02:00–06:00 UTC window for production cohorts.
- Observability: Ensure traces, kernel telemetry, and dispatch sampling are enabled and sampled at 100% for canary runs.

Metrics and observability contract
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 (token-gen and end-to-end). Baseline p95 for indexed canary must be recorded before experiment start.
- Error signals: 4xx/5xx surface on API, scheduler-retries, kernel-timeouts.
- Kernel signals: kernel-handoff-duration, kernel-eviction-count, kvcache-warmup-latency.
- Recovery metrics: time-to-first-successful-request, number-of-revert-attempts, rollback-latency.

Experiment matrix (templates)
| Variant | Perturbation | Target | Expected impact | Safety threshold |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| A | Slow context-switch (add 50–200us jitter to kernel scheduler) | kernel-shim | Increased p95, potential backpressure | Stop if p95 > 2x baseline |
| B | Partial KV cache corruption (drop 1% of prefetch hints) | kvcache-agent | Increased cold starts, cache warmup | Stop if kvcache-warmup-latency > 5x |
| C | Cooperative-preempt stall (simulate one cooperative preempt stall per node) | runtime-scheduler | Head-of-line blocking | Stop if queue-length > 10x |
| D | Randomized slow kernel calls (10% of calls delayed by 5ms) | kernel-shim | Microburst tail latency | Stop if error rate +0.5% absolute |

Pre-run checklist (every execution)
1. Create an experiment ticket referencing this runbook and link to monitoring dashboards.
2. Snapshot baseline metrics (last 24h) and attach to ticket.
3. Ensure alerting runbooks are assigned and primary/secondary on-call are notified.
4. Verify canary routing policy to route exactly N% traffic to canary cohort.
5. Validate inferno-guardian is configured with appropriate thresholds and test kill-switch in a dry-run mode.

Step-by-step run procedure
1. Staging validation
   a. Deploy kernel perturbation to staging cluster with same config as planned for canary.
   b. Run synthetic user traffic generator (inferno-sculpt) for 30 minutes.
   c. Collect traces, perf profiles, and kernel telemetry.
   d. Run automated post-check script: ./tools/inferno-postcheck --baseline <snapshot> --report out/report-staging.json
   e. Proceed to canary only if staging report passes all checks.

2. Canary deployment
   a. Deploy perturbation to canary nodes (1% traffic cohort).
   b. Start a 15-minute warmup with low traffic to let kvcache stabilize.
   c. Increment to full canary load and start continuous monitoring.
   d. If guardrails are violated, inferno-guardian will trigger a rollback; document the event.

3. Production cohort expansion (optional)
   a. Expand in 1% increments with 15-minute observation windows.
   b. Stop expansion if any safety threshold is breached.

Rollback and recovery procedures
- Automated rollback (preferred): inferno-guardian reverts kernel-shim to previous image and triggers a rolling restart of kernel-shim pods. Monitor rollback-latency and p95 recovery.
- Manual rollback steps:
  1. Pause traffic to affected nodes: kubectl label nodes <node> inferno-paused=true
  2. Revert kernel image: kubectl set image daemonset/kernel-shim kernel-shim=redwood/runtime-kernel:stable-20260501
  3. Trigger graceful eviction: kubectl rollout restart daemonset/kernel-shim --grace-period=60
  4. Run reconciliation: ./tools/kvcache-reconcile --nodes <node-list> --force-resync
  5. Unpause traffic when metrics show p95 within 10% of baseline for 10 minutes.

Operator commands and snippets
- Run the inferno-guardian dry-run locally:

```bash
# dry-run will simulate threshold breaches but not revert
python infra/inferno_guardian.py --experiment inferno-2026-05 --dry-run
```

- Deploy kernel-shim perturbation image (canary):

```bash
kubectl set image daemonset/kernel-shim kernel-shim=redwood/runtime-kernel:inferno-canary-2026-05
```

- Post-check example (JSON output):

```json
{
  "p95_before_ms": 120,
  "p95_during_ms": 280,
  "error_rate_delta": 0.002,
  "kvcache_warmup_factor": 3.1
}
```

Alerting rules to validate before start
- runtime.p95.above_baseline_multiple (alert if p95 > 2x baseline for 5m)
- runtime.api.error_rate.spike (alert if error rate uplift > 0.5% for 3m)
- scheduler.queue.length.high (alert if average queue length > 10x baseline)

Escalation path
1. On-call SRE gets page.
2. If automated rollback fails, call runtime-owner (pager) and handoff to emergency kernel team.
3. If rollback succeeds but residual errors persist > 30 minutes, open a Sev2 and follow incident runbook.

Post-experiment analysis and required artifacts
- Attach to experiment ticket: staging report, canary logs, full perf traces, tracer flamegraphs, kprobe captures.
- Required evaluation:
  - Fidelity delta report (sample prompts vs baseline)
  - Cost impact analysis (per-token CPU/GPU trend during perturbation)
  - Root-cause hypothesis and next steps (actions to harden scheduler or kvcache)

Ownership and RACI
- Responsible: runtime-ops (execution), kernel-shim eng (perturbation code), SRE (monitoring & rollback orchestration).
- Accountable: Head of Serving Runtime.
- Consulted: Security (for risk acceptance), Product (if customer-impacting).
- Informed: Customer Success for enterprise customers in cohorts.

Common failure scenarios and quick mitigations
- Scenario: KV cache warmup never completes
  - Mitigation: Revert perturbation, run kvcache-reconcile, and increase prefetch multiplier.
- Scenario: Scheduler preempt stall causes head-of-line blocking
  - Mitigation: Evict affected slots, escalate to kernel-shim team to toggle cooperative preempt flag.
- Scenario: Inferno-guardian fails to revert automatically
  - Mitigation: Manually trigger rollback and mark guardian incident for follow-up.

Postmortem template (to copy into ticket)
1. Title and experiment id.
2. Timeline of events with timestamps.
3. Metric deltas vs baseline.
4. Root cause hypothesis.
5. Action items (owners and due dates).
6. Lessons learned and prevention steps.

Appendix: injector config examples
- Sample injector YAML (staging):

```yaml
injector:
  perturbation_name: slow-context-jitter
  target_component: kernel-shim
  jitter_us: 120
  occurrence_rate: 0.05
  rollout_strategy:
    mode: canary
    canary_percentage: 1
    step_delay_minutes: 15
```

- Example monitoring query (Prometheus):

```
# p95 latency during experiment window
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```
